title: Complete the physical ordinary-interchange wrapper
body:
I join Nick Petalas's PR2808 outer wrapper to the fixed-role reversed caller in PR2809. I compute stock and widths on binary tapes, initialize minimal word templates without decoded widths, emit the selected unweighted ROOT, and preserve outer ownership through two separately padded calls. I erase the owned templates, markers and parking state before return, and add binary rectangle completion.

In PROOF.md I derive the completed ordinary binary contract O_q(V E^(1-a)) time and O_q(V)+F_q space, retaining a=169711/10^8. I use the pinned caller's written endpoint, chronology, refinement and cost arguments. The borrowing identity, stock formula, fit threshold and exponent arithmetic belong to the predecessors; I claim no new exponent or selected frontier.

Reviewers can reproduce:

```sh
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/physical-ordinary-interchange
```

All eight registered commands passed under Python 3.12.15/macOS arm64 after merging main `a1bfbc677fdcbc2a27a9b3bf6c78cac8fd6da9e2`. They cover encoded setup, actual selected unit-ROOT parsing, constructor/ownership controls, binary rectangles, and fitted/fallback/fitted reuse of one physical inventory. I check each padded F return before wrapper cancellation and every independent input column of the finite fixtures. A final binary-to-fitted-native case exercises all three allocation scopes together. RESULT.json pins complete typed receipts; VALIDATION.md records the replay and its limits. I claim no Linux or hosted-CI pass.

The fitted payload fixtures use a reduced q=2 grammar and explicit interface parameters. I have not executed the selected GL64 payload, expanded its complete transition table or supplied proof-assistant verification. The all-width statement covers successful admitted execution, not recovery from an interrupted inner macro. A stronger successor still needs a replacement for PR2753's decorated-key header route; a leaf-only substitution retains O(wV) routing.

I preserve exact source archives and credit Nick Petalas, David Arias, ywz65, Aakash (@aakashthakkar), commdata2338, the selected-word/source527 lineage and their retained notices. PR2888 provides adjacent stock-fit arithmetic; I do not repackage that coefficient result. I used substantial OpenAI Codex assistance and claim no independent human review.

[Canonical scope and evidence](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/2319#discussioncomment-18963568).
